## From Survey to Workflow

What the survey told us people want from tools:

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- **Easy to use**, even for less technical collaborators
- **Affordable and long-lasting**, without needing an institutional license
- **Customizable**
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
- **Interoperable** across tools and institutions
- **Synchronous editing and version control**
- **Safe data** handling, with a preference for **open source**
:::
::::

::: {.callout-box}
So we asked: for each step of a big team science project, *what tools already exist?*
:::

::: notes
Bridge from Francis's survey results. The takeaway: there are a lot of tools for a lot of things, and people often don't know about the alternatives. We built a map.
:::

## How We Built the Map

- Started from the "101 Innovations" research workflow (Kramer & Bosman, 2016)
- Adapted the stages for large, distributed, multi-site collaborations
- Drafted a first list, then had the working group react, comment, and edit in a shared HackMD doc
- **Still a work in progress, and we want your input**

::: notes
Be transparent: the first-pass table was AI-assisted to give the group something to react to. Specific packages may be too narrow; the group's comments shaped what's here.
:::

The data stages are where multi-site projects feel the most pain: harmonizing across sites, naming conventions, data dictionaries. Validation tools like ShinyValidator and Frictionless catch problems before they reach the central dataset. R codebook packages include codebook and dataReporter.
:::

::: {.column width="33%"}
**10. Dissemination & impact**

[Identity & citations]{.subhead}

[ORCID]{.chip .free} [Google Scholar]{.chip .free} [Scopus]{.chip .paid} [Web of Science]{.chip .paid}

[Attention]{.subhead}

[Altmetric]{.chip .freemium}

[Post-publication]{.subhead}

[PubPeer]{.chip .free} [Retraction Watch Database]{.chip .free}

:::
::::

::: {.legend}
[open source]{.chip .open} [free]{.chip .free} [freemium]{.chip .freemium} [paid / institutional]{.chip .paid}
:::

::: notes
Choosing a journal: JANE matches your abstract to journals that publish similar work; DOAJ lists open access journals; TOP Factor rates journals' open science policies; Open Policy Finder (formerly Sherpa Romeo) shows publisher self-archiving and funder open access policies. The working group suggested looking beyond CRediT to other contributor taxonomies (e.g., ScoRo, TaDiRAH) and listing field-specific preprint servers. HackMD and the other writing tools are tomorrow's topic. Post-publication: the Retraction Watch Database is now free through Crossref. Shout-out to FORRT (a BTSCon organizer) and its Replication Database for checking whether findings have replicated.
:::

## The OSF Question

OSF now mainly offers registries. What replaces everything else it used to do?

| OSF function | Possible alternatives |
|--------------|-----------------------|
| Project hub / wiki | GitHub, STAPLE, HackMD, Notion |
| File storage & sharing | Institutional storage, Dataverse, GitHub |
| Archiving with a DOI | Zenodo, Dataverse, Figshare |
| Preregistration | PreReg (ZPID), Zenodo (time-stamped), ClinicalTrials.gov, PROSPERO |
| Preprints | PsyArXiv, field-specific servers, Zenodo |

::: notes
This came straight from the working group. Many networks are asking this right now.
:::

## Underused Tools We Want You to Know

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- [**STAPLE**](https://staple.science/): project management built for research teams
- [**ShinyValidator**](https://github.com/manybabies/ShinyValidator): checks that each site's dataset is in the right format so they can be combined
- [**Psych-DS**](https://psychds-docs.readthedocs.io/): a community data standard for behavioral science datasets
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
- [**Datapages**](https://datapages.github.io/): templates for interactive dataset websites on GitHub Pages
- [**ResearchBox**](https://researchbox.org/): one organized box per paper for open materials
- [**HackMD**](https://hackmd.io/): collaborative markdown
:::
::::

::: notes
Overall message: there are many tools, and many good ones are under the radar. ShinyValidator, Datapages, and HackMD get the spotlight tomorrow.
:::

2. What would you use to replace **OSF**?
3. What **stops you** from adopting a new tool?
4. Which tool would you want a **tutorial** on? Would you lead one?
